content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To diagnose fibromyalgia, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Document widespread pain index (30 minutes)
Step 2. Evaluate sleep disturbance patterns (1 week)
Step 3. Perform manual tender point examination (20 minutes)
Step 4. Review patient history of cognitive "fibro fog" (1 hour)
Step 5. Conduct complete blood count (1 day)
Step 6. Assess comorbid irritable bowel symptoms (2 days)
Step 7. Screen for co-existing depression or anxiety (1 hour)
Step 8. Test for rheumatoid factor to rule out RA (3 days)
Step 9. Measure erythrocyte sedimentation rate (2 days)
Step 10. Finalize the diagnostic summary report (2 hours)
Step 11. Monitor morning stiffness duration (5 days)
Step 12. Rule out polymyalgia rheumatica (4 days)
Step 13. Perform antinuclear antibody (ANA) screening (4 days)
Step 14. Check thyroid stimulating hormone levels (2 days)
Step 15. Calculate symptom severity scale score (30 minutes)
Step 16. Assess for paresthesia or tingling (15 minutes)
Step 17. Evaluate response to initial lifestyle changes (4 weeks)
Step 18. Document history of chronic fatigue (1 hour)
Step 19. Consult with a physical therapist (1 hour)
Step 20. Track symptoms in a daily pain diary (2 weeks)
Step 21. Review family medical history (45 minutes)
Step 22. Map localized pain regions (15 minutes)
Step 23. Perform neurological reflex testing (30 minutes)
Step 24. Conduct Vitamin D deficiency screening (3 days)
Step 25. Rule out electrolyte imbalances (1 day)
Step 26. Investigate history of physical trauma (30 minutes)
Step 27. Evaluate for myofascial pain syndrome (1 hour)
Step 28. Assess current medication side effects (45 minutes)
Step 29. Verify symptoms have persisted for 3 months (3 months)
Step 30. Conduct differential diagnosis for lupus (1 week)
Step 31. Perform grip strength testing (10 minutes)
Step 32. Schedule initial rheumatology consultation (2 weeks)
Step 33. Rule out multiple sclerosis via MRI (1 day)
Step 34. Screen for obstructive sleep apnea (2 days)
Step 35. Evaluate autonomic nervous system function (2 hours)
Step 36. Assess sensitivity to light and sound (30 minutes)
Step 37. Test for Lyme disease antibodies (5 days)
Step 38. Review systemic inflammation markers (1 day)
Step 39. Evaluate bladder sensitivity and frequency (3 days)
Step 40. Document history of migraine headaches (1 hour)
Step 41. Conduct a tender point palpation (15 minutes)
Step 42. Conduct preliminary patient intake interview (1 hour)
Step 43. Review psychiatric history (1 hour)
Step 44. Rule out inflammatory arthritis (1 week)
Step 45. Check for Vitamin B12 deficiency (2 days)
Step 46. Rule out hypothyroidism (2 days)
Step 47. Screen for Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (1 hour)
Step 48. Evaluate for restless leg syndrome (3 days)
Step 49. Summarize all laboratory findings (4 hours)
Step 50. Administer the Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (20 minutes)
Step 51. Assess for chronic pelvic pain (45 minutes)
Step 52. Rule out hepatitis C (3 days)
Step 53. Evaluate for postural orthostatic tachycardia (4 hours)
Step 54. Perform a skin prick test for small fiber neuropathy (1 hour)
Step 55. Evaluate muscle enzymes like creatine kinase (2 days)
Step 56. Provide patient education on the diagnosis (1 hour)
Step 57. Assess for temporomandibular joint disorder (30 minutes)
Step 58. Collect initial patient blood samples (15 minutes)
Step 59. Review cognitive impairment levels (30 minutes)
Step 60. Evaluate for Raynaud’s phenomenon (1 day)
Step 61. Screen for chemical sensitivities (1 hour)
Step 62. Order a comprehensive metabolic panel (2 days)
Step 63. Review history of childhood stressors (1 hour)
Step 64. Assess for hypermobility (15 minutes)
Step 65. Test for C-reactive protein levels (2 days)
Step 66. Finalize Widespread Pain Index (WPI) data (15 minutes)
Step 67. Confirm clinical diagnosis of fibromyalgia (30 minutes)
Step 68. Rule out myositis (3 days)
Step 69. Evaluate environmental triggers (1 hour)
Step 70. Assess for Sjögren’s syndrome (4 days)
Step 71. Perform a physical gait analysis (30 minutes)
Step 72. Screen for chronic fatigue syndrome (2 days)
Step 73. Review history of neck or back injuries (30 minutes)
Step 74. Conduct a standardized tender point count (20 minutes)
Step 75. Rule out iron deficiency anemia (2 days)
Step 76. Review all exclusionary criteria (1 hour)
Step 77. Evaluate for overlap with other pain conditions (2 hours)
Step 78. Collect patient's prior medical records (2 weeks)
Step 79. Screen for sensory processing issues (1 hour)
Step 80. Determine the total Symptom Severity (SS) score (1 hour)
